one_line_contribution: A counterfactual bank-construction study on agent trajectory memory: it plants or removes near-duplicates of the test instance in banks of fixed size and asks (i) whether top-k retrieval has any residual over the best static prompt when no near-duplicate exists, (ii) whether the gain lives in the near-duplicate's instance-specific bindings rather than its procedure (redaction ablation), and (iii) whether the same near-duplicate, physically present in a whole-bank long context, goes unused and increasingly so as the haystack grows.
closest_prior_work: Bertsch et al., 'In-Context Learning with Long-Context Models' (arxiv:2405.00200, verified via s2cli/HF, 2024-04-30) is the closest pre-emption of the mechanism: it already shows long-context ICL gains come from attention to similar examples rather than cumulative task learning, i.e. that a many-shot context behaves like retrieval over its own contents. The proposal cites it and correctly notes it is on classification, not trajectory exemplars or task success, and that it predicts full in-context recovery -- so the proposal's P3 is a directed disagreement with a named prior, which is legitimate. Two closer threats on the reader side are NOT cited and are exactly the papers the proposal's own P3/P4 manipulations replicate. NoLiMa (arxiv:2502.05167, verified) removes the literal lexical match between needle and query and shows degradation that grows with context length -- which is precisely the r=1h 'hidden needle' (instruction line templated, body intact) manipulation, transposed to trajectories; the proposal presents this as a novel decoupling of retrievability from use without acknowledging that the finding it expects is NoLiMa's. And arxiv:2601.20276 ('Beyond the Needle's Illusion', verified, 2026-01-28) decouples evidence *access* from evidence *use* under semantic interference on a 326M-token memory bank and concludes semantic discrimination, not context length, is the bottleneck -- which both anticipates the access/use split that P3c and P4 are built on and argues against the proposal's own framing of P3b as a haystack-*size* effect. Neither kills the proposal, because neither runs an agent trajectory bank, task success as the outcome, or a retrieval-vs-whole-bank contrast at matched budget; but together they reduce the headline to a domain transfer of a known reader-side result, and their absence from the collision check is a real gap, since both surfaced on the automated novelty card the proposal was handed.
strongest_objection: The headline P3b does not hold what it says it holds fixed, and the gate biases the headline toward confirmation. (1) The proposal repeatedly asserts the size contrast runs 'with the distractor composition held fixed' and 'fillers identical at both sizes ... so only the count varies'. That is false as constructed. Each r=1 bank carries five needles, one per cluster instruction, at both sizes. For any single test instruction, one needle is its own and the other four are near-duplicates of its cluster siblings -- high-similarity hard negatives, not fillers. At size 12 those four are 4 of the 11 non-target items (36%); at size 40 they are 4 of 39 (10%). The size-12 whole-bank arm therefore has 3.6x the density of high-similarity distractors, and WB-12 minus WB-40 confounds haystack size with hard-negative density. The proposal knows this matters -- P6 exists precisely because sibling-like items displace the needle. The confound runs against the prediction, so a confirmation survives, but a null or a small effect is uninterpretable, and the title's 'Bank Size x Near-Duplicate Rate' factorial is never actually run: at r=1 the needle count is pinned at five, so near-duplicate rate (5/12 vs 5/40) moves with size by construction. (2) P1a gates the entire design on RET-40 r=1 minus r=0 reaching at least 15 points, and that same cell pair is the denominator of P3a's recovery fraction and sets P2's 5-point, P4's one-third/two-thirds and P6's 7.5-point margins. Conditioning on a noisy quantity clearing a threshold selects its upward fluctuations, so every recovery fraction reported afterwards is mechanically deflated and every margin inflated -- a winner's curse built into the pre-registration, pushing directly toward confirming the headline 'recovery below 0.5'. (3) No needle-position control. The whole-bank prefix is cached per cluster, so each of the five needles sits at a fixed depth and each test instruction's own needle sits at a different depth; position effects in long-context reading are well documented (arxiv:2605.27105, arxiv:2601.20276), and nothing in the design separates 'the reader cannot find the needle as the haystack grows' from 'this instruction's needle happened to sit deeper in the 40-item prefix'.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, roughly in order of importance. (a) Split-sample the gate: measure the P1a gain on one half of the clusters and use the other half as the denominator for P3a and as the source of P2/P4/P6 margins, so the confirmatory contrasts are not scaled by a quantity selected for being large. (b) Make the size contrast honest -- either hold the per-instruction haystack composition genuinely fixed (one target needle plus sib-0 fillers only, sibling needles moved out of the bank so cluster-mates are run as separate banks), or run the actual 2x2 by varying needle count with size (e.g. WB-40 with ~17 needles matched to WB-12's rate) and report size and rate as separate factors. Also randomise or counterbalance the needle's position in the whole-bank prefix across seeds and report recovery by depth decile; a per-cluster cache that fixes depth is the wrong trade against a headline about findability. (c) Add the random-k arm (see missing_baseline) so the retrieval-vs-whole-bank gap is not a mixture of selection and dilution. (d) Take the entailment check's P4 fix: score P4a as an absolute paired point difference against a threshold at least twice the re-measured subset floor rather than a ratio of two noisy differences, and pre-select body-retrievable needles so h is near 1. Separately: cite and position against NoLiMa (2502.05167) and 2601.20276 rather than presenting r=1h and the access/use split as new, and reconcile with EvoMemBench (2605.18421, verified), which reports long-context baselines outperforming specialised memory methods -- the opposite sign to P3 on a neighbouring question.
missing_baseline: A per-episode random-k selection arm drawn from the same r=1 bank, at matched tokens and matched (uncached) prefix status -- RANDOM-2 r=1. The brief's own Appendix B and gaps G12/G22 demand a random-selection control, and the track's title is 'When Does Experience Memory Need a Query'; RET-40 r=1 minus RANDOM-2 r=1 is the direct measurement of what the query buys with the bank held fixed, and it is the only arm that separates 'the needle is what matters' from 'two same-category items at this token budget are what matters'. The plan has fixed-2 (identical for all clusters, cached) and RET r=0, neither of which is a random draw from the needle-bearing bank, so the design's central contrast RET-40 r=1 vs WB-40 r=1 varies both what is shown and how much context surrounds it, with no arm in between. Two required cells are also simply absent: the abstract claims that without near-duplicates 'retrieval, the whole bank and the best static prompt are within the noise floor at every bank size', but RET-12 r=0 and RET-12 r=1 (sib-0) are not in the WebShop count list -- the retrieval size curve exists only in the 2-seed hard-negative cells (RET-12/40 r=1hn), so the paper's title claim about how retrieval scales with bank size rests on exploratory-grade arms.

(7) --recent: 'counterfactual ablation of retrieved exemplar content which part carries the benefit masking entity bindings keeping procedure' -> 2604.05467 (CUE-R, perturbs individual retrieved items to measure their operational utility in RAG) is the nearest analogue to P1b's redaction, on documents not trajectories; no collision. (8) --recent: 'does the whole memory bank in a long context match top-k retrieval for LLM agents matched token budget task success' -> nothing running that contrast on trajectory banks. IDs verified with s2cli paper or exact search hits: 2306.07863, 2405.00200, 2412.16926, 2411.07130, 2411.05000 (Needle Threading -- the proposal's gloss is accurate), 2607.26497 (BM25 Wins at Scale -- accurate), 2603.18272 (Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents -- accurate), 2601.20276, 2502.05167, 2605.18421, 2608.25500. Not verified (not load-bearing for novelty, but asserted in the proposal's check): 2510.16809, 2502.09933, 2608.20707, 2511.12997, 2410.03450, 2601.02744, 2406.13632. Judgement on the proposal's own check: it is better than most -- it names its queries, reports an honest empty result for its first phrasing, gives IDs for what came back, and states 'no pre-emption' rather than 'novel'. But it has a specific blind spot that matters here: it never searched needle-in-a-haystack vocabulary, despite the proposal being named after a needle and despite P3/P4 being NIAH manipulations. That omission is why NoLiMa (2502.05167) and 2601.20276 -- both on the automated novelty card handed to the author -- are absent, and both sit directly on the reader-side mechanism the headline claims. The line 'Revisions 1 and 2: no new method or citation introduced; no new queries run' is also a weakness rather than a neutral: the collision check was frozen while the design changed.
